# Plan: cache profile summaries in one process

> Reviewed by `/plan-ceo-review` on 2026-09-10, mode HOLD SCOPE. Original plan
> text is preserved below. Accepted amendments are marked `[A1]`..`[A5]` inline
> and defined in the review's Decision Registry. Nothing else in scope changed.

## Measured problem and accepted scope
The existing profile-summary service has one active process. A one-week trace
shows repeated reads of about 900 hot keys: DB CPU is 70%, with read p95 120 ms.
Add a process-local LRU wrapper to the existing repository. Acceptance targets
are at least 60% cache hits, DB CPU below 50%, and read p95 below 60 ms, with the
existing error-rate and correctness SLOs unchanged. This is an internal backend
change with no UI, API, schema, pricing, or developer onboarding change.

## Existing contracts retained
- All reads and writes use this repository in the same process; there are no
  external DB writers. Multi-process operation remains unsupported and startup
  rejects that configuration while caching is enabled.
- Authentication and authorization run before repository access. Keys encode
  the authenticated tenant ID and validated profile ID without ambiguity.
  Values are immutable profile-summary DTOs; secrets and cache keys are never
  logged. Cached results cannot bypass authorization.
- The existing LRU adapter supports 1000 entries, a 16 MiB byte cap, and a
  30-second TTL. Recorded hot data fits those limits. Absent records use a
  distinct sentinel with a 10-second TTL; undefined means a cache miss.
- Cache operations are synchronous and atomic in the single JS event loop.
  On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty
  cache is reinitialized; repository errors keep the current typed API error
  mapping. The existing per-key
  single-flight wrapper coalesces simultaneous misses and releases on failure.
- A read already in progress when a write commits may return its earlier DB
  snapshot to that caller. Every read begun after that write completes must
  observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute for this rule.
  **(Consistency invariant, unchanged. Review finding F1 shows the original
  sketch below did not meet it; amendment [A1] repairs the sketch.)**

## Proposed wrapper integration
Keep the current read-through repository interface and shared adapters.

**Original sketch (superseded by [A1]/[A2], retained for the record).** It
stated: "no additional version checks or coordination between a cache fill and
a write are proposed."

```javascript
// ORIGINAL — violates the consistency invariant (see F1 schedule S2)
async function readProfile(key) {
  const cached = cache.get(key);
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached;
  const value = await repository.read(key);
  cache.set(key, value);
  return value;
}
async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  const saved = await repository.write(key, update);
  cache.delete(key);
  return saved;
}
```

**Amended ordering rules [A1][A2][A4].** A fill may land only if no write for
that key completed after the fill's DB read began. Write completion (success or
failure) invalidates, in one synchronous tick: the cache entry, the in-flight
fill slot, and the single-flight slot, so later callers start a fresh DB read.

```javascript
/*
 * Fill/write ordering (keep this diagram current with the code):
 *
 *   R1 miss ─┐ await read (V0) ──────────────┐ resolve: slot gone → DROP fill
 *   W        │   await write ── commit V1 ── delete entry + forget slot (sync)
 *   R2 ──────┼───────────────────────────────┴─ begins after W: miss → fresh read → V1 ✓
 */
async function readProfile(key) {
  if (!flag.enabledFor(key)) return repository.read(key);       // [A4] deterministic per-key bucket
  const cached = cache.get(key);
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached;                       // includes ABSENT sentinel
  return inflight.run(key, async (slot) => {                     // existing single-flight, now slot-aware
    const value = await repository.read(key);                    // may resolve after a commit
    if (inflight.current(key) === slot) cache.set(key, value);   // else stale fill dropped, metric++
    else metrics.increment('profile_cache.stale_fill_dropped');
    return value;
  });
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  if (!flag.enabledFor(key)) return repository.write(key, update);
  try {
    return await repository.write(key, update);
  } finally {                                                    // [A2] success, typed failure, or indeterminate
    cache.delete(key);                                           // same tick: entry,
    inflight.forget(key);                                        // fill slot + single-flight slot
  }
}
```

`inflight.forget(key)` is a new method on the existing single-flight wrapper.
It drops the current slot so joiners arriving after the write start a fresh
read; callers already joined keep the in-progress promise (they began before
the write completed, which the invariant permits).

## Verification and rollout
Existing repository contract tests cover tenant isolation, key validation,
absence, DB failures, and authorization. New wrapper tests cover hit/miss,
eviction and byte limits, TTL, adapter-failure fallback, successful-write
invalidation, ~~failed-write preservation~~ **failed-write invalidation [A2]**,
and concurrent-miss coalescing.

Added by review (each is a required assertion, see Section 6):
- **[A1] Stale-fill ordering tests** with controlled pause/release points for
  schedules S2, S3 and S4 in the Async Ordering record.
- **[A2] Indeterminate write test**: write rejects after the DB has committed;
  the next read returns the committed value.
- **[A4] Flag transition tests**: read/write bucket agreement per key; any
  flag change clears entries and in-flight slots; flag evaluation error
  resolves to bypass.
- **[A5] Clock injection**: TTL and sentinel-TTL tests use an injected clock.

The rollout uses the existing runtime feature flag: enable for 10% of keys,
then 50%, then all keys after one healthy hour at each stage. Bucketing is a
deterministic hash of the key, evaluated identically in read and write [A4].
Monitor hit/miss, eviction, cache bytes, fallback errors, DB CPU, and read p95
without raw IDs. **[A3]** Also emit `stale_fill_dropped`, `set_rejected_oversize`,
`flag_eval_error`, and the gauge `cache_bypass_active`; alert when bypass is
active for more than 5 minutes or hit rate is below 60% for 15 minutes after
the 100% stage. Bypass entry logs at WARN with the adapter error class only.
On error-rate or latency regression, disable the flag immediately; both reads
and writes bypass the cache while disabled, and enabling creates an empty cache.
**[A4]** Any change to the flag value or bucket percentage reinitializes an empty
cache and clears in-flight slots; a flag evaluation failure resolves to bypass.
Cold starts remain within the existing DB capacity. The service owner monitors
the rollout and records the results against the acceptance targets.

## Out of scope
Distributed caching, cross-process coherence, prewarming, changing consistency
semantics, or adding new product surfaces. The repository interface preserves a
future replacement path without introducing a general cache framework now.

### Async Ordering Record (Section 4)

Shared state: `cache[key]`, `inflight[key]`. Invariant boundary: a read that
*begins* after `writeProfile` resolves must return the committed version.

```
  Sched | R1 (miss, reads V0)        | W (commits V1)              | R2 (begins after W) | cache[key] | Result
  ------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------|------------|-------
  S1    | read→set V0                | write→delete                | miss→read V1→set    | V1         | OK
  S2*   | await read ...             | write commits, delete(noop) |                     | -          |
        | resolves V0 → set V0       |                             | hit → V0            | V0 (30 s)  | VIOLATION
  S2 A1 | resolves V0, slot gone→drop| delete + forget (one tick)  | miss→read V1→set    | V1         | OK
  S3*   | await read ...             | write, delete               | joins R1 → V0       | -          | VIOLATION
  S3 A1 | await read ...             | delete + forget             | new slot→read V1    | V1         | OK
  S4*   | miss on absent → await     | create commits              | hit ABSENT (10 s)   | ABSENT     | VIOLATION
  S4 A1 | slot gone → drop ABSENT    | delete + forget             | miss→read V1        | V1         | OK
  S5    | begins before W, joins     | delete + forget             | —                   | —          | OK: R1 began before W completed (permitted clause)
```
`*` = original sketch. Mechanism preventing S2–S4 after [A1]: the forget and
the slot comparison run in synchronous ticks; no await separates `delete` from
`forget`, and no await separates the slot check from `cache.set`.

Shadow paths for the new flow (nil key, empty key, upstream error): nil/empty
keys are rejected by existing key validation before the cache; upstream read
error releases the slot and maps to the typed API error with no fill; upstream
write error invalidates per [A2]. All three covered by existing contract tests
plus [A2].

No user-visible interactions: interaction edge-case table not applicable.

misses); S2/S3/S4 with paused read return V1 to the post-write reader (rejects

adapter throw yields DB value and gauge=1 (rejects a thrown error); eviction at

clock; flag off skips both cache calls; flag change empties cache and slots.

adapter throws mid-fill while a write commits. Load test: 900-key replay at
10x, assert hit rate ≥ 60% and no DB call amplification.
